messages:
Maya: uploaded a perfetto trace from the nightly e2e run, looks like an interesting latency tail spike around request 8423. link: https://ui.perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (open to anyone)
Raj: skimmed it — client->gateway spans look normal but runtime span has a ~120ms hiccup. kernel timeline shows a cluster of small kernels interleaved with a large aten::matmul-like op.
Sam: is this the KV-cache miss pattern again? last time we saw interleaving when prefix hits dropped.
Maya: KV hit rate dropped during the spike: prefix hits 94% -> 58% for that window. I pulled kvcache counters from the trace (see bottom-of-trace counters).
Olivia: pasted the nsys summary I captured on the same run: 
```
==NV SYS PROFILE SUMMARY==
GPU activities:
  total gpu time: 1.24s
  top kernel: fused_attention_fp16  0.48s (38.7%)
  aten_matmul               0.31s (25.0%)
  kvcache_lookup_cuda       0.12s (9.7%)
```

smaller kernels show high enqueue/launch overhead.
Raj: looks like kernel selection flipped to aten_matmul variant mid-request — maybe sequence length heuristics misrouted to slow matmul path even though attention kernel would be faster here.
Tim: repro steps I used: 
```
# record perfetto
PERFETTO_RECORD=1 ./bin/runtime --trace=perfetto.pb --trace-events=client,gateway,runtime --workload=chat-mix --seed=8423
# then upload: curl -F file=@perfetto.pb https://perfetto.upload/
```

Sam: batch behaviour note — the gateway batched these as 8, but one request had a long prefix KV lookup (cache miss for first prompt chunk) which pushed it into a slow path and blocked the rest in the batch. Suggest capping batch wait to 12ms for this route.
Maya: screenshot of perfetto slice: span ids: client:0x7f1, gateway:0x7f2, runtime:0x7f3 — runtime shows repeated kvcache_lookup_cuda calls that coincide with CPU blocking on epoll.
Olivia: I also saw increased memcpy D2H around those kernels (nvtx region NAME=copy_d2h). nvprof snippet: 
```
MemcpyDtoH  0.048s  200 calls  avg 240us
```

Tim: with batch skew we get serialization: one slow request's KV thrash causes others to wait on the same worker. Maybe move KV lookup to async prefetch thread to avoid blocking producer-consumer on GPU worker.
Raj: I dumped the kernel selection logic logs (debug level) during the run — it selected aten_matmul when seq_len_estimate > 1024, but our trace shows seq_len_estimate=980 for the offending requests (off-by-one from tokenizer heuristics). We should make threshold conservative (1100) and add hysteresis.
Maya: action items: 1) run perfetto with kv-prefetch branch to see reduced D2H, 2) adjust selection threshold to 1100 + hysteresis, 3) experiment with batch wait cap 12ms for chat-mix route.
perf-bot: deployed perf regression alert for model-x at 2026-03-17T09:12:43Z (incuid=pr-1498). Relevant traces auto-linked.
Sam: I'll spin a dev build with async-prefetch and run same perfetto scenario, dropping a small script to reproduce.
Olivia: small helpful delta: when I forced kernel path to fused_attention via env OVERRIDE_KERNEL=fused_attention it reduced p95 from 92ms -> 56ms on the perf trace. Worth doing short-term fallback.
Tim: can we add a lightweight probe that measures kvcache prefix hit rate per-request and tags perfetto slices? would help triage automatically.
Maya: agreed — adding counters and a small microtrace annotation is next. I'll attach the collected trace and nsys outputs to the ticket.
Raj: nice work everyone. if Sam's async-prefetch fix replicates we'll ship a canary and monitor per-route prefix hit + tail latency. :thumbsup:
